THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 27.11.2021 passed in MVC.No.219/2020 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Sira (for short 'the tribunal').

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Sira
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
2. Though this matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsels for parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.
4. Brief facts of the case are as under:

On 29.04.2019 at about 3.00 p.m., one Jagannath was walking as a pedestrian,
during which time, near Palleshwara Swamy Temple, Sira town, a Maruti Omni Van bearing registration No.KA.40.M.5407 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the pedestrian, Jagannath, who sustained multiple fractures and Rajalakshmi vs Gangadhararadya M C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55702240/
2 injuries to all over the body.

He was immediately shifted to Government Hospital,
Sira.
But, unfortunately, on the way to the District Hospital, Tumakuru, he succumbed to the injuries.

4.1 It is stated that the deceased Jagannath was working as a Carpenter and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/-
per month.
Due to the sudden and untimely death of deceased Jagannath, the claimants, who are the wife and two children of the deceased, filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
On service of notice, respondents appeared and filed their separate written statement.
Respondent No.1 pleaded that the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and therefore, any liability i.e. fastened on him would have to be indemnified by respondent No.2.

Whereas, respondent No.2 denied the claim of the claimants including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the Maruti Omni Van and also pleaded that the driver of the said vehicle did not possess a valid and effective Driving Licence as on the date of occurrence of accident and that he has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by not obtaining fitness certificate.
On these grounds, sought for dismissal of the claim petition urging several grounds therein.
4.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed the relevant issues for consideration.
4.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P24.
On the NC: 2024:KHC:14942 other hand, the respondents neither examined any witness nor got marked any document.

4.5 On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsels for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.22,30,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation within one month.
4.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
5. Learned counsel for appellants-claimants submits that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, he seeks to enhance the compensation.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company sustains the judgment and award of NC: 2024:KHC:14942 the tribunal and contends that the tribunal has rightly awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants-claimants and learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company and perused the impugned judgment and award, Exs.P1 to Rajalakshmi vs Gangadhararadya M C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55702240/
3 P14 are the Police records, which depict registering of FIR and laying of charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, which is not challenged or disputed by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the negligence is rightly attributed as against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The claimants have also produced other documents as per Exs.P15 to P24 namely, aadhar cards, Bank passbooks, RTC extracts etc. in support of their case.

8. Now coming to the age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the tribunal has taken the age of the deceased at 48 years on NC: 2024:KHC:14942 the basis of Ex.P18-employee identity card, which shows age 41 years of the deceased as on the year 2012.
However, it is vehemently contended by learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the deceased was aged 45 years as per Ex.P5-inquest and Ex.P6-P.M.report.
Therefore, he contends that the age to be taken as 45 years instead of 48 years.

Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contends that Ex.P18-employee identity card produced by the claimants themselves belongs to the deceased and the details are furnished at the behest of the deceased showing his age as 41 years in the year 2012.
The accident occurred in the year 2019 + 7 years would be 48 years.
Hence, on this basis, the tribunal has taken the age as 48 years.

I do not find any cogent reason to differ from the opinion expressed by the tribunal with regard to the age, as the onus is upon the claimants to substantiate the age by producing cogent material to satisfy the Court that the age is lesser than 48 years.
Hence, the age is taken as 48 years.
The tribunal has taken the income at Rs.16,000/- per month, which also is based on Ex.P18-employee identity card issued by the Labour Office, Tumakuru.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was a carpenter by profession and the identity card is produced at Ex.P18.
It is the case of the claimants that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
However, no documentary proof is produced in proof of his income.
The fact remains that in an unorganised sector, the Court cannot expect a person to have necessary document in proof of his income.

Hence,
the occupation is identified and established.

In an unorganised sector, the Court will have to do a guess work for assessment of income, which has to be just and reasonable for assessment of compensation especially in the road traffic accident cases.

Even if Rs.700/- is taken per day as income, which is normally earned by a skilled workers in an unorganised sectors like carpenter,
plumbers, painters, the income per month would be Rs.18,200/-.

Hence, the income is NC:
2024:KHC:14942 rounded off to Rs.18,000/- per month as against Rs.16,000/- as awarded by the tribunal.
10. The tribunal has added 25% towards future prospects to the income and deducted 1/3rd, in view of there being three dependants, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.

Therefore, the claimants would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.23,40,000/- (Rs.18,000/- x 25% = Rs.22,500/- - 1/3rd = Rs.7,500/- = Rs.15,000/- x 12 x 13 = Rs.23,40,000/- as against Rs.20,79,948/- awarded by the tribunal.
11. The tribunal awarded Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of spousal and parental consortium, which does not call for interference.

However, 10% escalation for one block period on the same is to be Rajalakshmi vs Gangadhararadya M C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55702240/
4 awarded under this head, which would come to Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.1,20,000/- + 10%).
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:14942 12.

The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards transportation and funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate, in all, Rs.30,000/- is awarded, which does not call for interference and the same is retained and 10% escalation for one block period on the same to be awarded, which would come to Rs.33,000/- (Rs.30,000/- + 10%).

13. In view of the above, the claimants would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.25,05,000/-
as against Rs.22,29,948/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of dependency 23,40,000-00 Loss of consortium 1,32,000-00
Transportation and funeral 33,000-00 expenses and loss of estate  TOTAL 25,05,000-00 13.
